an3.52:1.1: Then two brahmins who were old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, come to the last stage, a hundred and twenty years of age, approached the Blessed One … and said to him:
an3.52:1.2: “We are brahmins, Master Gotama, old, aged … a hundred and twenty years of age.
an3.52:1.3: But we have not done anything good and wholesome, nor have we made a shelter for ourselves.
an3.52:1.4: Let Master Gotama exhort us and instruct us in a way that will lead to our welfare and happiness for a long time!”
an3.52:2.1: “Truly, brahmins, you are old, aged, burdened with years, advanced in life, come to the last stage, a hundred and twenty years of age,
an3.52:2.2: but you have not done anything good and wholesome, nor have you made a shelter for yourselves.
an3.52:2.3: Indeed, this world is burning with old age, illness, and death.
an3.52:2.4: But though the world is burning with old age, illness, and death, when one has departed, bodily, verbal, and mental self-control will provide a shelter, a harbor, an island, a refuge, and a support.”

an3.52:3.4: not the one that is burnt inside.
an3.52:4.1: So since the world is ablaze
an3.52:4.3: one should take out by giving:
an3.52:4.4: what is given is well taken out.

an3.52:5.4: and the deeds of merit one did while alive, lead to one’s happiness.
